articles.title: Al Tottenham le han perdido el respeto
articles.standfirst: Su cuota para descender a Championship ha caído hasta los 8.0 en Bwin
articles.summary: Su cuota para descender a Championship ha caído hasta los 8.0 en Bwin
articles.body: El Tottenham estuvo a punto de protagonizar uno de los grandes descalabros del fútbol inglés la temporada pasada. El conjunto londinense consiguió esquivar el descenso a Championship en la última jornada... pero apenas unos meses después vuelve a encontrarse en una situación comprometida. El equipo de Roberto De Zerbi se ha marchado al primer parón de selecciones como colista de la Premier y las apuestas deportivas ya empiezan a reflejar una pérdida de confianza evidente. La situación resulta especialmente llamativa teniendo en cuenta el esfuerzo realizado durante el verano. De Zerbi, el gran artífice de la salvación del curso pasado, pidió refuerzos para cambiar la dinámica del equipo y la directiva respondió entregándole 10 fichajes por un valor de 366 millones de euros. Sólo Manchester City y Chelsea gastaron más en el mercado estival. Sin embargo, las piezas todavía no terminan de encajar y el Tottenham apenas ha conseguido sumar dos puntos en las cinco primeras jornadas. Sus primeros goles de la temporada llegaron el pasado fin de semana, en la derrota contra el Aston Villa, y el equipo ya ha igualado el peor inicio de su historia. Además, fue eliminado a las primeras de cambio de la Carabao Cup. Las mejores casas de apuestas también han tomado nota de este preocupante comienzo. El desplome de la cuota para el descenso, de 51.0 a 8.0 en Bwin, refleja hasta qué punto ha cambiado la percepción alrededor del Tottenham en apenas unas semanas. El club ha pasado de considerar el mercado como una oportunidad para construir un proyecto ambicioso a volver a mirar de reojo la pelea por la permanencia. De Zerbi tendrá ahora el parón de selecciones para trabajar con mayor margen y tratar de encontrar soluciones, mientras que la confianza de la directiva en el técnico sigue siendo máxima. El italiano necesita tiempo para conseguir que todas las piezas encajen, pero el calendario tampoco parece dispuesto a conceder demasiada tregua. A la vuelta del parón, el Tottenham visitará Old Trafford para enfrentarse al Manchester United. Un partido que, eso sí, guarda un recuerdo especialmente agradable para los londinenses, puesto que conquistaron la Europa League en 2025 tras imponerse al conjunto mancuniano en la final. Bwin, sin embargo, paga a 4.5 la victoria del Tottenham en esta ocasión. Una cuota que refleja la dificultad del desafío. El duelo ante el Manchester United puede convertirse en el punto de inflexión que necesita el Tottenham para empezar a recuperar terreno y, sobre todo, volver a ganarse el respeto de la Premier. De Zerbi todavía cuenta con el respaldo de la directiva y tiene por delante una plantilla construida a golpe de millones para cambiar la situación. Pero, si los resultados no llegan y el equipo mantiene el rumbo actual, el club podría verse obligado a apretar el botón rojo.

articles.title: ESPN Cameraman Called Out For His Zooming In On Saturday
articles.summary: He's been called out by many.
articles.body:
An ESPN cameraman trended on Saturday afternoon for his apparent zooming in during the Florida vs. Ole Miss game.

During Florida's win over Ole Miss, an ESPN cameraman chose to zoom in on the Gators crowd, as a blonde fan in a black dress stole the show on X, formerly known as Twitter, on Saturday afternoon.

"Camera man knew exactly what he was doing 😭😭😭," one fan joked, as the clip of the zooming in received millions of views on X.

"The look of a guy that knows exactly what's behind him, and has spent the whole game knowing there's no smooth way to just turn around and look," one fan joked.

"And so did she… I hope mom and dad are proud of their spawn," one fan added.

"SEC it just means more," one fan added.

Florida impressed, though head coach Jon Sumrall remains unsatisfied with the Gators.

"Really proud of our guys. Still have a lot to clean up. But the responses tonight, I thought we started fast. I thought we got off the field on third down early in the game defensively when maybe some momentum wasn't going our way in the third quarter. I thought our guys, the kick returns, a couple of those were huge in maybe resetting the tone of the game. The forced fumble was a big deal," he said postgame.

"That quarterback's [ Trinidad Chambliss ] an unbelievable player. And so for our guys to maybe I think keep him off balance at times, that's the least uncomfortable I've ever seen him look, and he's kicked my butt as a head coach twice last year. And so watching him today, I thought our guys affected him. That No. 1 is a really good player for them."

Florida improved to 4-0 on the year with the win over Ole Miss.

articles.title: Florida Gators, Mississippi State soar, USC tumbles in latest inexplicable AP Top 25 Poll
articles.summary: The Florida Gators surged 13 spots to No. 8 in the AP Top 25 poll after demolishing Ole Miss, while Missouri's puzzling ranking fuels SEC bias debate.
articles.body: One of college football's greatest traditions got another entry on Sunday, as the week four edition of the AP Top 25 Poll was released to mostly bemused reactions from confused fans. And if there was any doubt that the SEC continues to enjoy some, uh, questionable, benefits based on preseason polling and perceived strength, this week's voting should put that to rest. Unsurprisingly, one of the biggest gainers of the week was the Florida Gators, coming off an impressive 52-28 win over the Ole Miss Rebels. Florida racked up over 300 yards on the ground, forced two turnovers, and kept the ball away from Trinidad Chambliss and the powerful Ole Miss offense. After what could be a season-changing win, the Gators moved up a whopping 13 spots to No. 8, one spot ahead of the Rebels. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Oklahoma State Cowboys were another big mover, jumping 11 spots to No. 19, as their win over the Oregon Ducks looks even better after OU's win over USC. UCLA , too, moved 14 spots into the top 25 at No. 23 thanks to a 54-3 obliteration of the Maryland Terrapins. Another surprise team through week four? The Mississippi State Bulldogs, who held on to beat Missouri and moved up eight spots to No. 16. But speaking of Missouri, they exemplify the problem that the preseason poll and voters' pre-conceived biases have with these rankings. The Tigers entered the season as the No. 25 team in the preseason poll and proceeded to do literally nothing of importance in the first three weeks. A 54-21 win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff, a 38-21 win over a bad Kansas team, and a surprisingly close 27-17 win over an atrocious Troy team. Their reward was to move up to No. 19 heading into the game against the Bulldogs, which resulted in the 31-24 loss. Somehow, after again, looking very unimpressive for the entirety of the season, Missouri sits at ... No. 25 in the week four poll. That's the exact type of SEC-specific outcome that fans from other conferences complain about. Look bad, do nothing, lose, stay right where you were. And then brag about the number of "ranked games" and "ranked wins." Meanwhile, Missouri has not beaten an SEC team that finished the season with a winning record since 2024 and their wins that season were over 7-6 Arkansas and 7-6 Vanderbilt. articles.title: “An F”: Caitlin Clark accepts failure as Indiana Fever crushed by Aces in A'ja Wilson's 38-point showdown
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark kept her postgame review short. Asked to grade the Indiana Fever defense, she said, \"An F.\" Few could argue.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark kept her postgame review short. Asked to grade the Indiana Fever defense, she said, "An F." Few could argue.The Las Vegas Aces took the first-round opener 102-85 on Sunday, and A'ja Wilson did most of the damage with 38 points and 16 rebounds. Indiana now has one game left to keep its season alive, and the defense needs a lot of work before then.Why Caitlin Clark gave the Fever defense an F in Game 1Caitlin Clark's grade came after the Fever allowed 102 points on Sunday, and the numbers back it up. Las Vegas shot 59 percent overall and 47 percent from three. It was one of those nights when nearly every possession ended in a clean look.Wilson was the center of it all. The reigning WNBA MVP hit 15 of 19 shots and tied a playoff career high with 38 points. She also pulled down 16 rebounds, blocked four shots, stole the ball twice, handed out two assists and knocked down two threes. Indiana had no real answer for her.The Fever guard had a rough night at the other end too. Clark scored 15 points on 6-of-17 shooting, though she did add 10 assists for a double-double. Kelsey Mitchell struggled even more, hitting 4 of 16 for 12 points. Aliyah Boston led Indiana with 18, and Sophie Cunningham chipped in 13 off the bench. It was not enough to keep pace with an Aces offense that barely missed.Raven Johnson gives Caitlin Clark and the Fever one bright spotIndiana lost backup guard Tyasha Harris to a season-ending leg injury in the last regular-season game. Coach Stephanie White had said before the playoffs that rookie Raven Johnson could help fill the gap. She did.Johnson played 22 minutes off the bench in the postseason debut and scored 14 points on 6-of-7 shooting. She added two steals, an assist and a three-pointer. The two-time NCAA champion at South Carolina looked comfortable on a night when few teammates did. White said Johnson "did great" and gave the team the lift it needed on both ends.Clark, the newly crowned AP Comeback Player of the Year, was just as impressed with the 5-foot-8 rookie. She liked the offense, but she singled out the defensive intensity as exactly what Indiana needs from here on. In her view, Johnson puts in the work and can be counted on.Now the margin is gone. Game 2 is Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, with tipoff set for 6:30 p.m. ET. A second loss ends the Fever's season. articles.title: “Kind of mirrors the inequality”: How Naomi Osaka’s $32 billion crypto deal turned into an $11 billion investor lawsuit after the company collapsed
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka joined a major cryptocurrency company as a global ambassador in March 2022.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka joined a major cryptocurrency company as a global ambassador in March 2022. The deal gave the tennis star an equity stake in a company valued at about $32 billion. Eight months later, the company filed for bankruptcy, and Osaka was named in an $11 billion investor lawsuit.The lawsuit also named major sports and entertainment figures, including Tom Brady, Stephen Curry and Gisele Bündchen. Investors accused the celebrity promoters of helping bring customers to the platform. The case later changed as the court dismissed most of the claims against the celebrity defendants.Naomi Osaka took an equity stake and wanted more women in cryptoOn March 21, 2022, the cryptocurrency exchange announced Osaka as a global ambassador through a long-term partnership. She received an equity stake in the company and compensation in cryptocurrency. She also agreed to help create content and promote the platform to a global audience.The partnership had a specific goal. Osaka wanted to help bring more women into crypto, an industry that had a much smaller female presence at the time.“We have seen the statistics about how few women are part of crypto by comparison, which kind of mirrors the inequality we see in other financial markets,” Osaka said in the March 21, 2022 partnership announcement.She also spoke about making cryptocurrency easier for more people to access.“Cryptocurrencies started with the goal of being accessible to everyone and breaking down barriers to entry,” Osaka said in the same announcement.Her role went beyond putting her name on a sponsorship. Osaka helped direct and produce promotional content and wore the company's logo during competition, starting with the 2022 Miami Open. The company also said she would invest and trade cryptocurrencies of her choice.The partnership arrived when the company was expanding rapidly across sports. It had secured naming rights to the Miami Heat's arena and signed several high-profile athletes and celebrities.Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, Stephen Curry and Larry David were among the other familiar names linked to its marketing campaign. Osaka became part of that push while the company carried a reported $32 billion valuation.In Osaka's case, the deal added another major endorsement to an already strong business portfolio. Sportico estimated her 2022 earnings at $53.2 million, with about $52 million coming from endorsements, according to Tennis.com.Then the company's financial problems surfaced.The sudden collapse brought Naomi Osaka into the $11 billion lawsuitOn November 11, 2022, the cryptocurrency exchange filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Four days later, investors filed a class-action lawsuit in Florida seeking $11 billion in damages. The complaint named Osaka along with Brady, Bündchen, Curry, Shaquille O'Neal, Larry David, Shohei Ohtani, Trevor Lawrence, David Ortiz, Kevin O'Leary and others.The investors argued that the celebrity promotions helped bring customers to the platform. The complaint specifically pointed to Osaka's promotional work and her equity stake.The lawsuit also quoted Osaka's promotional video, in which she said, “I’m Naomi Osaka and I’m proud to partner with FTX. Making cryptocurrency accessible is a goal that FTX and I are striving towards.”However, the lawsuit's allegations did not establish that Osaka knew about any alleged fraud inside the company.The legal case changed significantly in 2025. On May 7, U.S. District Judge K. Michael Moore dismissed 12 of 14 claims against the celebrity defendants. The judge found that investors had not shown the celebrities knew the company was fraudulent or that receiving promotional payments alone proved a conspiracy. Some claims under Florida and Oklahoma law remained.Osaka therefore was not ordered to pay $11 billion. The timeline tells the bigger story. Osaka entered the partnership on March 21, 2022, when the company had a reported $32 billion valuation. On November 11, it filed for bankruptcy. Four days later, investors named Osaka in their lawsuit.A partnership built around expanding women's access to cryptocurrency had suddenly become part of the legal fallout from one of the biggest collapses in the crypto industry.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. All Elite Wrestling announced on social media on Sunday night that Benjamin Satterley had died at 40. Then came Sunday's brief, heartbreaking announcement.PAC cause of death: what is known so farBenjamin Satterley's death was announced by AEW on Sunday night, first through its social media accounts.The questions are loud because the calendar is so tight. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans."Until AEW, his family or an official source says more, any explanation is a guess.Beyond the PAC cause of death: a career built on high-flying offenseSatterley started in the ring in 2004 and spent the 2000s building a name on the international circuit. articles.summary: Connor McDavid has never forgotten the impact Ben Stelter had on Edmonton. In Jan.
articles.body: Connor McDavid has never forgotten the impact Ben Stelter had on Edmonton. In Jan. 2026, the Oilers captain returned to a school fundraiser supporting the late superfan’s foundation. His wife, Lauren Kyle, has taken a different path into community work. She serves on the Edmonton Oilers Community Foundation board, which helps children access sports. Together, their charity work reaches young people through two different causes. Connor McDavid keeps Ben Stelter’s legacy aliveOn Jan. 27, 2026, McDavid visited Allendale School in Edmonton after the junior high won the Ben Stelter School Fundraiser. Fifty schools joined the campaign, which raised more than $285,000 for the Ben Stelter Foundation.Speaking at Allendale School, McDavid said, “I think kids helping kids is a special thing.” He then highlighted the wider community effort behind the fundraiser.“I hope the one thing they take away is the power of community and what together we can all do for each other to help one another,” McDavid said at the January 2026 event.The connection dates back to 2022. Stelter died from glioblastoma on August 9, 2022, at age six. During the 2021-22 NHL season, he became a familiar face around the Oilers and Edmonton after the team welcomed him into its community.McDavid has continued supporting the foundation created in Stelter’s name. At Allendale School, he explained why its work remains personal.“This is important to me because Ben and the Stelter family is important to me,” McDavid said at the fundraiser.He also highlighted the foundation’s help for families dealing with childhood cancer, including dream experiences, medical equipment and cancer research. In September 2025, she hosted a charity poker tournament supporting Every Kid Deserves a Shot.That gives the couples two distinct charitable paths. articles.standfirst: Benjamin Satterley, que competía bajo el sobrenombre de PAC en la AEW y Neville en la WWE, falleció con 40 años
articles.summary: Benjamin Satterley, que competía bajo el sobrenombre de PAC en la AEW y Neville en la WWE, falleció con 40 años
articles.body: El luchador Benjamin Satterley, que competía bajo el sobrenombre de PAC en la AEW (All Elite Wrestling) y Neville en la WWE (World Wrestling Entertainment), ha muerto de forma repentina con 40 años apenas un día después de pelear en el NOW Arena de Chicago (Illinois). El fallecimiento del popular PAC, que se produjo una noche después de su último combate en el evento de pago por visión 'All Out' contra el campeón nacional, fue comunicado por la AEW. Hasta el momento, no se ha confirmado oficialmente la causa del fallecimiento. "All Elite Wrestling lamenta anunciar el fallecimiento de Benjamin Satterley, también conocido como PAC. Oriundo de Newcastle (Inglaterra), Satterley comenzó su carrera en la lucha libre en 2004 y compitió para organizaciones de todo el mundo, cautivando a los aficionados con innovadores movimientos aéreos y una increíble habilidad sobre el cuadrilátero. PAC firmó con All Elite Wrestling en 2019; ostentó varios campeonatos de AEW y participó en algunos de los combates más memorables de la historia de la compañía. Nuestras condolencias a la familia, amigos y seguidores de Satterley" , compartió la AEW. Pac se convirtió en una figura destacada tras abrirse camino en el circuito independiente y unirse a la WWE en 2012. Durante sus seis años en la WWE, bajo el nombre de Neville, ganó el Campeonato de NXT y posteriormente fue conocido como el 'Rey de los Pesos Crucero' ('King of the Cruiserweights'), consolidándose como la principal figura de dicha división. Fue dos veces Campeón de Peso Crucero, incluyendo un reinado de 197 días —que en aquel entonces marcó un récord— y que incluyó varios combates memorables. Su combate por el Campeonato de la WWE contra Seth Rollins en 2015 fue uno de los mejores del año y se considera una de sus actuaciones más destacadas. Tras dejar la WWE a finales de 2017, se convirtió en uno de los primeros miembros de la emergente All Elite Wrestling en enero de 2019.

articles.title: Rams are only 11th team ever to lose the way they did vs. Broncos
articles.summary: The Rams racked up 482 yards and held the Broncos under 260, and still lost the game.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos beat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night, but it felt more like the Rams beat themselves. Los Angeles lost a heartbreaker, 30-26 , blowing a 16-point halftime lead by allowing 30 second-half points – including 14 points in the final 5 minutes.

Based on the box score, you wouldn't have thought the game was close. The Rams had the ball for 34:29 out of the 60 minutes, picked up 26 first downs, went 8-for-17 on third down and racked up 482 yards of offense on 82 plays.

The Broncos , meanwhile, had just 257 yards of total offense.

According to Stathead , the Rams are only the 11th team in NFL history to lose a game where they had at least 480 yards on offense and allowed fewer than 260 yards to their opponent.

The last team to lose such a game was the Bills in 2022, a 21-19 loss to the Dolphins , where they allowed only 212 yards and had 497 yards on offense. Before that game, the Texans ' 34-28 loss to the Ravens in 2010 was the last time.

They found ways to lose, whether it was with Matthew Stafford 's pick-six, their 13 penalties for 91 yards or the poor play on special teams.

articles.title: OTD (28/09/1989): Smith Takes Financial Gamble To Bring Star To Roker
articles.summary: With the clubs finances running low, Denis Smith takes a gamble with a big signing.
articles.body:
It probably goes without saying, but Sunderland AFC weren't in a good place when we dropped to the third tier of English football in 1987.

There was real potential of Sunderland staying down in the lower leagues for the long term. Young chairman Bob Murray had only recently taken over from Tom Cowie and had to deal with the fall out from the Lawrie McMenemy era. This also meant dealing with the financial impact.

McMenemy was on big money, and some of the players he brough to the club were as well. Then there was the state of Roker Park, which was crumbling and required a lot of TLC. Finances were tight and that meant the deal to bring in Denis Smith and Viv Busby from York City was in jeopardy when they demanded a fee of £20,000 for the pair.

Sunderland only got their man due to Smith suggesting he would pay the fee out of his own pocket if he didn't get Sunderland back into Division Two at the first time of asking – which he did.

Smith brough in some bargains to the club that included Marco Gabbiadini (£80,000), John Kay (£22,500), Colin Pascoe (£70,000) and John MacPhail (£23,000), and we not only won the Third Division title, but went on to consolidate in Division Two by finishing 11th in the 1988/89 season.

This raised expectation levels for the second season in the second tier, especially because we had flirted around the play-offs for periods before dropping off. This was dampened however, by the fact only Paul Hardyman was the only signing during the summer when he signed from Portsmouth for an eventual £130,000 that was set by a tribunal.

The season started well with a win at Swindon Town, but Ipswich Town came to Roker a few days later and won 4-2 to put us back in our place. Ahead of the third game against Middlesbrough Smith had secured another signing when Paul Bracewell arrived at Roker for a second time, this time from Everton on an initial one-month loan deal.

Bracewell had been superb in his year on Wearside before moving to Everton where he went close to completing the treble in his first season. His performances on that level resulted in Bobby Robson calling him up to the England squad and had it not been for an injury sustained at St James Park in a tackle with Billy Whitehurst, Bracewell would have no doubt played a lot more games for Everton and England.

As it was, he was looking to get back to full fitness and play again and gave his former Stoke City teammate Denis Smith a call to see if that could be at Sunderland. Smith jumped at the chance and Bracewell returned to the Sunderland midfield for a second time against Middlesbrough at Roker in a 2-1 victory.

Over the next few weeks Bracewell took us up another level and many clubs were linked with taking him on permanently, including Newcastle United who he faced for Sunderland in a goalless draw on the 24th September 1989.

The assumption was that Sunderland were not in a position to pay the money Everton were expecting or the wages Bracewell would require. articles.title: ‘The Régis Revolution’: Assessing Le Bris’ Impact At Sunderland
articles.summary: Calm, measured and charismatic…just how impactful has our French gaffer been at the Stadium of Light?
articles.body:
As we're currently in the midst of a very long and quite frankly pointless international break, now is a good time to reflect on the achievements of Régis Le Bris. After taking charge of his one hundredth game as Sunderland manager in the defeat to Manchester City , just how good has he been for Sunderland AFC ?

In the last decade, Sunderland has quite often been a basket case of a football club with lots of turnover of players and almost as much managerial turnover, too.

So often, a new season would start with optimism, new arrivals and a new manager at the helm backed by a full summer of transfers, only for us to start the slowly and end up in a relegation scrap as early as October or November.

A new manager would come in, inject a new lease of life into the playing squad and do just enough to keep us in the league. These were often appointments made with one objective: to keep us in the league.

Whilst the managers appointed to do these jobs achieved their objectives, they would be gone by the start of October of the following season and the merry-go-round would start over.

Even in the days of League One, a manager would come in to get us promoted and whilst unsuccessful in their first season, were given a second bite of the cherry the following season, but slow starts would lead to their dismissal and for someone else to take the reins.

This makes the achievement of Le Bris in reaching one hundred games all the more impressive.

The last Sunderland manager to reach this milestone would also achieve promotion in his first season in charge and would go on to have a successful first season in the Premier League. That man was Roy Keane all the way back in 2007/2008. Ironically, Keane left Sunderland with a very similar winning percentage as Le Bris' current Sunderland winning percentage.

After one hundred games in charge, Keane had managed 42 wins — exactly the same as Le Bris'. This is the best winning percentage of any Sunderland manager to complete a full season since Jack Ross in 2018/2019, also the last manager to complete a full season in charge of Sunderland before Le Bris.

What's made Le Bris' stint at Sunderland so impressive is the style of football he's been able to implement so quickly.

Something that made Alex Neil's League One promotion squad so successful was their defensive solidity and ability to pick up points without playing pretty football. The squad was already good enough to win games, but we were far too open at the back for us to be successful.

Under Tony Mowbray in the Championship, we had a young, exciting team that played with the handbrake off and looked to outscore teams but often with a lot of naivety at the back, yet Le Bris has found the perfect blend of these two successful teams.

We're largely solid at the back and it's incredibly hard for teams to break us down, especially when buoyed by the Stadium of Light crowd.

We're more than happy to sit in and soak up pressure in our own box whilst also being comfortable with the ball and turning teams over in transition, which won us a large volume of points last season. This was a perfect recipe for a newly promoted team and was a large factor in helping us achieve a seventh-place finish.

We're now starting to see a transition away from a more pragmatic style, and we're playing with the handbrake off a lot more often. This has left us more vulnerable at times but it's certainly something that was needed in order for us to try and progress even further this season.

Not since the turn of the century under Peter Reid has the club finished higher than tenth in the Premiership, with the only other top half finish being under Steve Bruce.

To do this in only your second season in English football and as a newly-promoted club is an unbelievable achievement. This was the first time a promoted club had gone on to qualify for Europe since Wolves did it under Nuno Espírito Santo in the 2018/2019 season.

All of this combined with the rate at which he's been able to achieve this in just two seasons at the club is almost remarkable in itself.

We often see managers coming into English football for the first time take time to adapt and get their ideas across, but Le Bris has taken to it like a duck to water and has only gotten better with every season. It only took him a few sessions in his first pre-season to work out his core group of players that would fit his system, and he stuck with this small group of seventeen or eighteen players throughout the season.

Let's not forget that the club underwent an overhaul of the squad in the summer following promotion, and alongside a lot of early business that was completed, Le Bris was able to bed these players in quickly over the course of pre-season, and we came flying out of the blocks.

The man has been an absolute breath of fresh air. He's bought into the culture and expectations of the club and the area, and has been nothing short of magnificent. He's also a calm head in amongst the chaos and he never lets his emotions get the better of him.

It's a compliment to his tactical nous that well-established figures like Enzo Maresca have publicly stated how difficult they have found it to manage against him and have been surprised by the tactical tweaks he's made in games in order to get that extra ons per cent over the opposition.

There have, of course, been one or two batterings along the way, but not even Pep Guardiola and Mikel Arteta are perfect!

articles.title: 5 key plays lead Broncos comeback victory over Rams
articles.summary: 2nd half chaos upends Rams on Sunday Night Football…
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams appeared to have control of Sunday's matchup against the Denver Broncos , but a series of pivotal plays helped Denver rally for a 30-26 comeback victory .

The Rams had opportunities to put the game away, but mistakes, a controversial penalty and two late interceptions ultimately swung the game toward Denver.

Here are five plays that played a major role in the Broncos ' comeback.

1. Emmanuel Forbes ' Unsportsmanlike Conduct Penalty on Special Teams

With just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter, the Rams appeared to have created a favorable special-teams situation. Denver's Kaden Katsis muffed the punt and recovered at the Broncos' 15-yard line before being tackled at the nine.

However, Emmanuel Forbes was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct. The 13-yard penalty was enforced from the previous spot, moving the Rams back and forcing them to punt again from their own 12-yard line. The second punt traveled to the Denver 48, giving the Broncos much better field position.

Instead of potentially pinning Denver deep after the muff, the penalty essentially gave the Broncos another opportunity with favorable field position.

The biggest swing came with 4:49 remaining.

Leading 19-16, Matthew Stafford and the Rams had a chance to grab more momentum after a poor third quarter showing. Instead, Stafford attempted a short pass toward Kyren Williams that was intercepted by Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga .

Hufanga did not simply stop the drive. He returned the interception 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver a 23-19 lead after the extra point.

The turnover was a huge momentum shift and injected life throughout the Broncos sideline and fanbase.

3. Bo Nix Finds Pat Bryant for 39 Yards on 2nd-and-20

Denver's offense delivered a huge conversion on its game-tying drive.

With 3:26 remaining and facing second-and-20 from the Denver 25, Bo Nix connected with Pat Bryant for 39 yards. Bryant took the pass all the way to the Los Angeles 36, flipping the field and keeping the Broncos' comeback hopes alive.

The play was particularly damaging because the Rams had Denver facing a long-yardage situation. Instead of forcing a punt or another difficult third-down attempt, Nix found Bryant for a chunk gain that put Denver deep into Rams territory.

4. Controversial DPI Call on Josh Wallace

A few plays later, the Rams appeared to come up with a potential stop.

On third-and-6 from the Los Angeles 11-yard line with 1:15 remaining, Nix's pass intended for Bryant fell incomplete. Josh Wallace was flagged for defensive pass interference, however, giving Denver four yards and an automatic first down.

The call was a clear miss. Not only was it an interception by Josh Wallace but replay showed that it was actually offensive pass interference (if anything) on Pat Bryant. Bill Vinovich strikes again…

From there, the Broncos were able to run additional clock and get the go-ahead score.

The Rams still had one final opportunity.

After Stafford connected with Konata Mumpfield for a 48-yard touchdown with 3:38 remaining, Los Angeles cut Denver's lead to 23-22. The Rams then needed one more defensive stop and a chance to complete the comeback themselves.

That opportunity came late, but Stafford's final pass was intercepted by Hufanga, who had already delivered the pick-six earlier in the fourth quarter. The turnover ended the Rams' final possession and secured Denver's comeback victory.

For the Rams, the loss wasn't determined by one play. The Forbes penalty, Stafford's pick-six, Bryant's 39-yard catch, the Wallace DPI and the final interception collectively created the sequence that allowed Denver to erase a late deficit and escape with a four-point victory.

articles.title: What's the best mascot in Cincinnati? We're letting you decide
articles.summary: Which local sports team has the best mascot? Here's your chance to vote for your favorite.
articles.body:
Best mascot in Cincinnati sports? It's gotta be one of these

When it comes to local sports rivalries, current traditions such as the Crosstown Shootout and the battle for the Victory Bell are the most notable. And sure, some of them have gone by the wayside – goodbye Bridge Bowl .

But we are giving you a fresh and unique opportunity to help give your favorite team some bragging rights over the competition.

It doesn't matter the size (or the sport, actually), because we are here to find Greater Cincinnati's top mascot. Pro or college doesn't matter. We are giving you the power to vote on who is your favorite.

Will the Reds' four different official mascots split the vote? And who'll come out on top of the catfight with the Bengals, FC Cincinnati, UC and Mount St. Joseph's mascots? Can the Cyclones' Twister knock down Florence's Y'all Star water tower?

Outside of the occasional broomball game these questions have gone unanswered for years. But now, the power is in your hands.

Vote below for your favorite local mascot in town, and keep scrolling to learn a little more about each one.

The Reds have four different official mascots: Mr. Red, Mr. Redlegs, Rosie Red and Gapper.

Mr. Red: First introduced as a live mascot in 1973 .

Mr. Redlegs: Similar name, but sports a retro mustache and uniform. Returned to team in 2007.

Rosie Red: Female mascot introduced in 2008.

Gapper: This furry mascot was introduced when Great American Ball Park opened in 2003.

Who Dey: The Bengal tiger, always decked out in his No. 1 jersey .

The Bearcat: A student began dressing as the mascot in the 1950s . Now recognizable in his No. 00 jersey.

D'Artagnan the Musketeer: First appeared in costume in the 1960s and bears a resemblance to its "Three Musketeers" namesake.

The Blue Blob: Larger, furrier alternative introduced in the 1980s.

Swoop the RedHawk: Made its debut after the school changed nicknames in 1997. (Once had a memorable "run in" with Kentucky's Jamaal Magloire during an NCAA Tournament game.)

Victor E. Viking: Was once named one of college basketball's 10 scariest mascots by ESPN .

Tommy Mo: Always there to fire up crowds whenever the Saints play.

Joe Lion: Pumps up the fans at MSJ events.

Not eligible, however, is the cicada Mount St. Joseph brough out for April Fools' Day in 2021.

Gary the Lion: Was introduced in 2019 before the club's first MLS season. (He got his name when the club released it's first logo and fans saw the name "G-A-R-Y" spelled out .)

Y'all Star: After rebranding from the Freedom to the Y'alls, the mascot made it's debut paying homage to the city's iconic water tower .

The Cyclones also have a pair of mascots.

Twister: The tornado is know for it's signature "F5" jersey.

Puckchop: The newer of the Cyclones' mascot. It pays homage to the city's Porkopolis roots .

The Flying Pig: This pig is ready to run in its marathon clothing and running shoes.

articles.title: Glamorgan welcome best ever Division One finish
articles.summary: Glamorgan captain Kiran Carlson says the team "would have bitten your hand off" at the start of the year to finish sixth in the Championship's top flight.
articles.body:
Glamorgan captain Kiran Carlson says the team "would have bitten your hand off" at the start of the year to finish sixth in the Championship.

It is the first time Glamorgan will play successive seasons in Division One after relegation in 2001 and 2005 - their only previous seasons in the top flight.

They were fourth starting the last block of fixtures, but suffered heavy innings defeats against Somerset and Warwickshire in early September.

"It feels like a big relief," Carlson said after the season-ending, rain-hit draw with Essex.

"It's nice to finish well, there was a moment we thought we could be in that relegation battle but [winning at] Surrey last week was a huge result, and to be able to put in a really good three-and-a-bit days against Essex was very pleasing."

The Welsh county were a surprise package earlier in the campaign, with home victories over Somerset and Surrey which saw them riding high, before three defeats and a precarious draw when the four-day competition resumed in late August.

"It's been a year of a lot of ups and downs in the Championship, especially a frustrating end to the year, but it's a testament to all the lads, the coaching staff and everyone around us that we've finished strongly in these last two games," said Carlson.

"Sixth is somewhere we're comfortable and something to build on for next year."

Coach Richard Dawson, who has worked with England Lions and was in the running for the senior England job mid-season, has steered Glamorgan to promotion and top-flight survival in his first two seasons without extensive big-name recruitment.

But he is keen to spread the praise for maximising the club's resources.

"It's a collective effort, a huge effort from everyone," he said.

"People stepped up. You never know if someone is ready until you put them in, so it's great when they stand up.

"It might not be a hundred or a five-for, but you see how they walk out and face up to an international player at the other end."

However, Dawson says the team needs to become more ruthless in 2027 to turn four-day draws into wins, and to win tight T20 games. They missed out on the knock-out stages for the ninth season running with a record of six wins from 12.

"It's having that ruthless edge to us in all formats. We've shown the skill level, but if you look at the four-day stuff, how [champions] Warwickshire finished the season off, they've been bang on every session," reflected the coach.

"I've looked at how Somerset went about their work when we went down there. In the T20 season, we didn't qualify, but I don't think that'll be too far away.

"People making match-defining innings or closing it out, it's about how consistent we can be under pressure."

For next year Glamorgan will be losing a total of 35 seasons of experience between the retiring trio of Chris Cooke (16 years with the club), Colin Ingram (11 summers) and Billy Root (eight).

Teenager Jack Hope-Bell could be the next batter in line for regular Championship exposure after two games in addition to a One-Day Cup run.

Meanwhile, Alex Horton scored heavily in the One-Day Cup and could be a leading name to replace Cooke, with Will Smale, Henry Hurle and Harry Wallace as other wicket-keeping options.

As well as replacing Ingram as the overseas batter, Glamorgan will have to try to tie down overseas bowlers, after using Ryan Hadley, Mir Hamza, Ray Toole, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Nathan McAndrew in that role during the four-day and T20 campaigns.

"Colin Ingram may be the last of an extinct breed, here from March to September. Ultimately we've got a spot opened up so we'll probably look to get an overseas top three, or opening batter to fill that gap we've got," director of cricket Mark Wallace told a members' forum.

"It is so difficult with the international calendar; it takes a lot of my time."

Meanwhile the 50-overs competition - where Glamorgan won two games out of eight - is being justified for its development role.

"We've taken the approach for the last few years to try to strike a balance between giving squad players and young players experience, and trying to make sure there's enough experience around them," said Wallace.

"The last player to be selected into the batting unit was Jack Hope-Bell, so if one of the more senior players played, Jack would have missed that debut hundred and that development, so it's a balance.

"Tom Norton was blooded in the 50-overs competition last year. We've used that with Ben Kellaway and Asa Tribe in the past."

Contract announcements for the remaining members of the men's squad, along with several current players and new signings for the women's team, are expected in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Seahawks Game Against Commanders Showcases Familiar Flaw
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks‘ loss to the Washington Commanders showcased a common issue that the team dealt with last season: turnovers, specifically from Sam Darno...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks ' loss to the Washington Commanders showcased a common issue that the team dealt with last season: turnovers, specifically from Sam Darnold and Jadarian Price. Seattle Seahawks quarterback Darnold threw two interceptions against the Washington Commanders in his first game back from the glute injury sustained against the New England Patriots . While Darnold overall had a good game, throwing for 379 yards and four touchdowns, the turnovers remain an issue in his profile.

In the fourth quarter, Darnold threw a pick six to Washington Commanders linebacker Kain Medrano .

Darnold said, "Bad decision. The end did a good job of not letting me escape to the outside, and had to make a quick decision. … Should've dirted it at his feet."

Similarly, rookie running back Price also coughed up a fumble in the first quarter, resulting in a soft-benching for most of the first half. He only carried the ball five times for 15 yards as the Seahawks failed to get their running game going. The Seattle Seahawks only averaged 2.4 yards per carry on 18 rushing attempts.

Price said, "I made a mistake early on, so just got to deal with the consequences that come with that."

Seattle Seahawks Sam Darnold and Jadarian Price Give Up Two Critical Turnovers Against Washington Commanders

Because of the deficit and script, the Seattle Seahawks had to make sure Darnold pushed the ball down the field. 71.8% of Seattle's offense involved the passing game. It was another excellent game for wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba , but tight end A.J. Barner and sophomore receiver Tory Horton also had great performances. Yet, the Seahawks offense seemed frustrated with their lack of consistency, relying on explosive plays.

Darnold said, "You got to tip your cap to those guys. They played a really good game defensively. All around, they played a really good game."

Similarly to last season's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , head coach Mike Macdonald finds himself dissatisfied with the key turnovers and defensive struggles.

He said, "I thought we threw the ball relatively well, but we got to take care of the ball as an offense."

Despite Two Key Turnovers, Darnold Still Had A Respectable Performance

The Seattle Seahawks locker room still has Darnold's back though as many would expect. There was no Ernest Jones post-game speech, but Cooper Kupp gave Darnold his flowers regardless of the result.

Kupp said, "But, man, to come back and do what he did — I mean, you got to realize this was his first game of the year. He played five plays (in Week 1). And so I thought he did a great job. It just seemed like the command was there. Made some great throws, scrambling in the pocket, extending plays."

Macdonald also came out of the game liking what he saw from Darnold. However, he stresses the importance of going back to the film and dissecting what happened. The Seahawks still believe in their process and aim to quickly correct what went wrong against the Commanders.

Macdonald said, "The takeaways are tough, but again, we'll look at them and see why [Darnold] made those decisions and what we can do to make better decisions. But I think on the whole, he kept us in the game."

articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays, on Sunday, ended the 2026 MLB regular season on a high note, taking a 5-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds in an emotional affair. Max...
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays , on Sunday, ended the 2026 MLB regular season on a high note, taking a 5-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds in an emotional affair. Max Scherzer , in potentially his final big-league start, threw seven innings of one-run ball. Moreover, George Springer grappled with some strong feelings as well as he navigated the possibility of facing Rogers Centre for the final time as a member of the Blue Jays .

Springer, who signed a six-year, $150 million contract with the Blue Jays prior to the 2021 season, will be headed to free agency this winter. There is also a possibility that, at 37 years of age, Springer chooses to retire — with injuries already having taken their toll on him.

With that in mind, Blue Jays manager John Schneider made it a point to give Springer a moment to bask in the adoration of fans on Sunday — with Schneider subbing him out for a pinch-runner in the bottom of the third after Springer hit a leadoff double.

"I think the world of George Springer , player, person … I wanted to make sure he had a moment with the fans cause he had so many huge moments here with us," Schneider said in his postgame presser, via Sportsnet on X.

This season was Springer's worst in the big leagues (according to fWAR), recording 15 home runs and 54 runs batted in on an OPS of .726 in 126 games.

It looked like Springer was in the middle of a sharp decline, as he recorded a total of 2.8 fWAR in 2023 and 2024 after he had a 4.0 fWAR campaign in 2022. But in 2025, during the Blue Jays' magical season, Springer had a revival — hitting 32 home runs and 84 RBIs with a stellar OPS of .959.

In Springer's six seasons with the Blue Jays , Toronto made it to the postseason thrice. They came to within two outs away of winning a World Series title before falling to the Los Angeles Dodgers in extra innings in Game 7 of the 2025 Fall Classic.

Springer will surely draw some interest on the open market, should he choose to continue his big-league career.

articles.title: Tommy Coyle will 'turn back clock' to fight again
articles.summary: Tommy Coyle and Derry Mathews will raise money for boxing clubs in Hull and Liveerpool.
articles.body:
Former Commonwealth lightweight champion Tommy Coyle will make his return to the ring to help raise money for charity.

Coyle, from Hull, hung up his gloves more than five years ago, but is set to box again against former opponent Derry Mathews to benefit boxing clubs in the city and Liverpool.

The 37-year-old said: "The response has been incredible. It's been humbling and I'm excited, but I'm a little bit nervous as well."

The fight is set to take place on 11 December at a venue, which is yet to be confirmed, in Hull.

Coyle and Mathews first battled for the Commonwealth title at Craven Park, Hull, in 2013. Mathews won in the 10th round.

Coyle said: "Who knows what's going to happen? In round 10, I got knocked out, so let's just see if I can turn back the clock.

"We're two old pros that are friends and we're going to go at it and try and create some memories."

Discussing his comeback, Coyle also reflected on the loss of his father Chris who died in 2022. He had been a "huge part" of his career.

"It will be the first fight my dad's not seen," said Coyle.

"It's sad, but I can't not do things just because he's not around anymore. He isn't coming back and I've had to learn to come to terms with that.

"I've really struggled with him not being around, he was my best friend.

"For the next 12 weeks, it will give me something to focus on, something to chase, and something to occupy my mind. If I say I'm doing something, I always do it."

Coyle added: "Boxing fans will be the winners in this fight as well as the clubs we're raising money for."

Jacoby Brissett is now 2-13 as the starting quarterback of the Arizona Cardinals.

Brissett Gives Honest take on Cardinals' Second Half Surge

"We cleaned up the operation and our focus and attention to detail got better in the second half. But, again, you can't give a good team a half."

This is simply a reflection of Arizona falling short in the attention to detail department, backing up what Brissett had to say. The 49ers took advantage of the Cardinals' lapses, and a good team ultimately seals a victory in these scenarios on average.

How exactly do Arizona and Brissett build on the loss?

Cardinals Must Take Advantage of Positive Week Three Momentum

Brissett went into week three of the season with his back against the wall. There were simply numerous sources of criticism from numerous groups coming his way following a rough week two performance.

Now, Brissett seems to be back on the right track. Sure, the 33-year-old signal caller found uneven returns early on in week three. Ultimately, the NC State alum managed to settle into the game, throwing for nearly 300 yards – as well as two touchdowns – in the process.

articles.title: Mexico tie Colombia in Rafael Marquez’s coaching debut
articles.summary: Mexico and Colombia tied 1-1 as they both opened their four year road to the 2030 World Cup.
articles.body:
Mexico battled back to earn a 1-1 tie against Colombia in the debut of Rafael Marquez as Mexico's National team coach. Mexico had a very good performance in a match where they were the slightly better team against an opponent who they have struggled against in recent times. Mexico bounced back from an early goal against to get the tie that starts the tenure in route to the 2030 World Cup. Mexico will travel to New Jersey where they will face Peru on Tuesday while Colombia will also travel to New Jersey where they will face off against Paraguay on Friday.

The 1st half started with the surprise that Hirving Lozano would get the start in his return to the National team. A cross into the area got badly headed by Armando Gonzalez and Colombia's goalkeeper, Alvaro Montero, would easily get to the ball. After making a great move, Richard Rios got off a great cross into the area where Luis Javier Suarez would get to it and head the ball past Mexico's goalkeeper, Raul Rangel , to score and give Colombia the early 1-0 lead. It was a good cross although defender Israel Reyes should have paid better attention to Suarez and not allowed to get that close range header. After getting the ball in the area, Lozano got off a left footed shot that forced a save from Montero. Mexico started to dominate possession as Colombia started to get more physical, with a number of fouls especially to Gilberto Mora . Erik Lira got off a right footed shot from outside the area that went well wide. Off a free kick, Luis Chavez got off a left footed shot that went just wide. Off a counter, the ball would be cleared into the path of Roberto Alvarado , who would get off a left footed shot that hit the post. The ball would rebound straight to Chavez, whose right footed shot from close range would hit the post and go wide in a bad miss in what should have been a goal. A cross into the area would find Lozano and Gonzalez, who would both go for the goal and Lozano's header would bounce off the post. Gonzalez would get off a left footed shot in the area that was saved by Montero. The halftime whistle blew and Colombia took a lead although Mexico had deserved to get the tying goal.

The 2nd half started with neither team making a change during the halftime break. A thru pass found Lozano, who got into the area in a 1 vs 1 but his right footed shot was blocked by Montero, although replays showed that he would have been offside and called off had he scored. A wide open Gonzalez got into the area and got off a horrendous shot that went wide and he was lucky to have been called offside in the play because it was a terrible attempt. Off a free kick, Jhon Arias got off a great right footed shot that forced a good save from Rangel. A great pass would find Gilberto Mora, who made a great move to get past Jhon Lucumi and then get off a right footed shot past Montero to score a fantastic goal to tie the match at 1-1. The teenage sensation made his first goal for the Senior National team and it was a great one. Mexico subbed out Hirving Lozano, Luis Chavez, Gilberto Mora and Jesus Gallardo for Orbelin Pineda , Obed Vargas , Alvaro Fidalgo and Mateo Chavez. Colombia subbed out Luis Javier Suarez, Alvaro Angulo and Andres Gomez for Kevin Viveros, Samuel Velasquez and Jaminton Campaz . A cross into the area was badly played by Rangel, who failed to get to the ball but Daniel Muñoz couldn't get a solid header on the ball and it went wide. Colombia subbed out Richad Rios and Kevin Castaño for Matias Orozco and Yaser Asprilla. Mexico subbed out Armando Gonzalez, Jorge Sanchez and Roberto Alvarado for German Berterame, Jeremy Marquez and Isaias Violante . A good 2 vs 1 chance was wasted when Fidalgo's pass would go long and Montero got to it easily. Violante got the ball in the area and got off a left footed shot that was easily saved by Montero. Mexico subbed out Erik Lira for Denzell Garcia. In the final minute, a scuffle happened between both teams in what ended up being the final play of the match as the referee blew the whistle as it died down. While Mexico once again failed to defeat Colombia, they were the better side in a good tie to start Marquez's tenure.

Rafael Marquez started his tenure in a great way with a very good tie against Colombia. Although a victory would have been preferable, the tie was a good result especially since Mexico had a good performance against a very good side. Mexico hasn't defeated Colombia since 2010 and recent results have been poor especially their last one, a friendly in 2025 where Colombia defeated Mexico by a 4-0 score. The early goal looked to make things tough for Mexico but they had key chances after it, where the better side and had a great moment with the tying goal by Mora. Gilberto Mora's goal made ripples thru the world of football as it was a great goal and the 17 year old showed he had arrived with his first goal in the National team. Mexico will hope to improve result wise on Tuesday when they will face a Peru side that needs to bounce back after losing on Saturday against the United States by a 4-1 score. Mexico should make a number of moves as not only a number of players from Liga MX will arrive but they will need to rest players as they will face two more friendlies, the most important being on Saturday against the United States, their biggest rival and a team that Marquez has history against.

Northern Ireland vs Hungary – Match preview and team news

These setbacks are highly likely to force tactical rotations, with midfielder Alex Toth pushing strongly for a spot in the starting eleven to inject creativity.

articles.title: Billy Monger urges the young to overcome self-doubt
articles.summary: Monger, who broke the Ironman record for a double amputee, urges the young to "chase their dreams".
articles.body:
"Social media could lead to doubtful self-comparisons," says Billy Monger - a man who has overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges before becoming a sporting champion.

The TV presenter and former racing driver from Charlwood in Surrey broke the Ironman record in 2024 after having both legs amputated following a near-fatal crash in 2017.

He now wants to offer the younger generation tips on overcoming life's obstacles.

"I would love to speak to youngsters about the value of trying different things and chasing your dreams," added Monger, who is now training for the Los Angeles Paralympics in 2028.

"Social media plays a big part in our lives," he says. "Yet it only shows people the end result of someone's achievement, not the journey it takes to get there."

Monger believes self-doubt can lead youngsters feeling as if they had not found their success or passion yet.

The 27-year-old recalled during his formative years, his passion for racing helped him find people with similar interests.

"At school, I often felt pressure to fit in. But I would like to say to kids don't let other people stop you from chasing your dreams," he said.

Monger - a former contestant on Strictly Come Dancing - has just released his first book, Find Your Drive.

He said he wanted to offer insights into his daily life beyond his public persona.

"People see snippets of my life on social media, documentaries or Strictly, but they don't always see the work and determination behind me overcoming my challenges after the crash ", he said.

"I hope to visit schools, including my former school, to share my book, talk about my experiences and encourage students to challenge themselves so they can learn more about who they are."

Monger is currently training to qualify for the triathlon event at the next Paralympic Games.

"It is an exciting event, and it's great that it's getting more attention," he says.

"However, I think parasports in general should have greater coverage so people can further appreciate the athletes' talents."

articles.title: ‘Can do without me’: Brock Bowers makes blunt admission after Raiders’ 3-0 start
articles.summary: Brock Bowers made a blunt admission after returning from injury to help the Las Vegas Raiders beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 and move to 3-0. The tight en...
articles.body:
Brock Bowers made a blunt admission after returning from injury to help the Las Vegas Raiders beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 and move to 3-0.

The tight end had missed the first two games of the season but wasted little time making an impact, catching 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown.

Bowers' return came as the Raiders continued their perfect start, with wins on the road in each of their last two games.

Brock Bowers admits Raiders can win without him after Saints victory

Speaking to "Raiders Gameday" after the victory, Bowers admitted he was not surprised by how well the offence had performed without him.

"I wasn't surprised about the offence the last two weeks," Bowers said. "They come out there, they execute every single day, and we got some great playmakers out there. As you can see, they can do without me. It was great to be back and flying around and being with the team."

Bowers also reflected on what it means to be 3-0, praising the Raiders for producing complementary football on both sides of the ball.

"… It feels amazing being 3-0. Going on the road the last two weeks, winning two tough road games. I think we're playing some good football both ways. Defence has been balling out, getting turnovers everywhere. So yeah, it's really just complementary football."

Kirk Cousins also praised Bowers after his first regular-season game with the quarterback, although he admitted the pair still have plenty of work to do together.

"He's an outstanding player," Cousins said. "Klint did a great job with the scheme, getting him opportunities. I'm still learning him. I would have to say that we don't have as many banked reps as I would like, but I think I can get accustomed to a guy like that pretty quickly."

Cousins finished with 248 passing yards and three touchdowns, while the Raiders overcame 27 points from New Orleans .

The challenge now gets tougher, with Las Vegas returning home to face the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 4.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark shares heated words for Aces fan after Fever’s costly Game 1 playoff loss
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark seemed to clash with a courtside fan during the Indiana Fever’s 105-82 loss to the Las Vegas Aces in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs. The Feve...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark seemed to clash with a courtside fan during the Indiana Fever 's 105-82 loss to the Las Vegas Aces in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs.

The Fever have to climb a mountain to keep their season alive, needing to beat the reigning champions in back-to-back games to advance to the second round.

With how uncompetitive the Fever looked in their Game 1 loss, it's no surprise that the players were leaving the court with a lot of frustration, which slipped out of Caitlin Clark toward a fan.

Caitlin Clark appears to send two-word message to Aces fan after loss

A fan in the stands at the Aces' Michelob ULTRA Arena shared a video of Clark , in which she can be seen angrily mouthing 'shut up' at a heckling fan in the crowd.

While it's unclear what the fan might have said to Clark to elicit this response, it is clear that the 24-year-old superstar was facing the brunt of their playoff loss and likely didn't appreciate whatever remark came from the fan.

This was a rough loss for the Fever, as they have to beat the Aces in back-to-back games to keep their season from ending in the first round of the playoffs.

Clark had a mixed outing in Game 1, scoring 15 points (6-17 FG) with 10 assists and six turnovers.

The Fever couldn't keep up with the Aces

Fever's leading scorer Kelsey Mitchell had a worse night with just 12 points on poor shooting efficiency, while the injured Aliyah Boston managed an efficient 18 points despite clearly not being at 100%.

The Aces used a three-headed monster to eviscerate the Fever defense, led by A'ja Wilson's incredible 38 points, 16 rebounds, two steals, and four blocks.

Jackie Young added 21 points and 10 assists for a double-double with three steals and six turnovers, while Chelsea Gray had an efficient 14 points, five rebounds, and eight assists.

The talent and schematic mismatch was too much for Indiana to overcome. Now, it's a question of whether they can make some magic happen and complete an improbable comeback to eliminate the Aces over Games 2 and 3.

Verlander's former Tigers teammate Max Scherzer was among those watching during his final game, as Verlander pitched 5.1 innings, gave up five hits and two earned runs, and fanned six batters. An Eduardo Valencia walk-off home run gave Tigers fans more to smile, and cheer about as they beat the Pirates 4-3 on September 26.

Verlander started the season with expectations of pitching well, early and often for manager AJ Hinch 's team after a strong season in 2025. At age 43 and dealing with injury problems, he wasn't able to muster up enough strength to pitch the way fans expected of him until the very end.

The longtime Tigers ace's performances with one of the MLB's most hallowed franchises will live on in the hearts and minds of baseball fans everywhere, from Cooperstown to Detroit, to Houston and the West Coast. Verlander has nothing left to prove, and plenty of time off to enjoy, now that he has completed one of the most exceptional careers in recent sports history.

articles.title: Could be a good omen: Klopp matches 60-year-old unwanted record
articles.summary: Two games, one point, and only third place in the Nations League table: If you look only at the results, Jürgen Klopp’s start as Germany head coach has been...
articles.body:
Two games, one point, and only third place in the Nations League table: If you look only at the results, Jürgen Klopp's start as Germany head coach has been a failure.

Of course, it should also be said that pure results are only of secondary importance given the current state of German football . The fact that Klopp tried out a great deal in his first two matches against the Netherlands (0:0) and Greece (0:1) and sent out a team that was largely unfamiliar with one another—also forgiven!

Still, it is more than just unusual for a Germany head coach to go without a single win in his first two games. The last time this happened was more than 60 years ago, when Helmut Schön managed only a 1:1 draw against Sweden and Italy in 1964.

One reason for optimism: that very same Schön went on to shape what was perhaps the best national team in the world in the years that followed. In 1972, he led Beckenbauer, Müller and co. to the European Championship title, before winning the World Cup on home soil in 1974.

Of course, we should not expect the current DFB generation to replicate that run of success. Still, the comparison between Klopp and Schön shows that good things sometimes take time...

articles.title: Not Zirkzee – Former Red thinks Man Utd must replace Amorim favourite with a ‘better option’
articles.summary: Manchester United have been told to find an upgrade on Mason Mount, who is currently playing second fiddle to Bruno Fernandes.The Red Devils spent £60 millio...
articles.body:
Manchester United have been told to find an upgrade on Mason Mount, who is currently playing second fiddle to Bruno Fernandes.

The Red Devils spent £60 million to acquire the England international from Chelsea in the summer of 2023.

Unfortunately for the attacking midfielder, his time in Carrington has been hampered by injuries, which have often derailed his momentum.

Louis Saha thinks Mason Mount isn't good enough for Man Utd

(Photo by Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

In Michael Carrick's 4-2-3-1 formation, Mount is considered a backup for Fernandes in the No.10. And since the Portuguese star is the club's captain and main talisman, the Englishman has to accept limited playing time.

But while Mount is seemingly at peace with his current role, Louis Saha believes it's time for United to find themselves an upgrade on the Chelsea academy product.

"Manchester United could have signed another playmaker to play as the second striker or a more creative midfielder who is a better option than Mason Mount to replace him," said the former MUFC striker in his interview with Betano (via Metro ).

"He is another good player, but he is not someone who is going to accelerate a game for Manchester United.

"He has been very unfortunate with injuries, but he has never shown me that he is that kind of player who in hot moments, is going to take the pressure and responsibility alongside Bruno Fernandes."

Why Mount can be an important asset for Man United

While Saha brings up a valid point by suggesting that Mount has seldom been decisive for United, the Portsmouth native was an absolute game changer when he first made his breakthrough at Chelsea.

At Man Utd, the Englishman hasn't been enough on the pitch to leave an indelible mark, whether due to injuries or the manager's hierarchy.

Nevertheless, Mount has always been appreciated by his MUFC coaches , especially Ruben Amorim, who reportedly tried to bring him to AC Milan in the summer.

As for Carrick, he entrusted him with a deeper role during pre-season. Mount's exploits in the double pivot alongside Andrey Santos sparked reports of INEOS abandoning the pursuit of the third midfielder, with the former Chelsea star permanently moved to central midfield.

In the end, these speculations proved wide of the mark, with Carlos Baleba joining the club. However, Mount's ability to cover several roles, rather than merely serving as Bruno's understudy, renders him a valuable player for the cause.

It should also be noted that Mount's late introduction against Fulham helped United raise their tempo, culminating in Matheus Cunha's equaliser.

articles.title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 30-26 victory over the Los Angeles Rams
articles.summary: There is A LOT to unpack from this up-and-down rollercoaster of emotions thriller that thankfully ended in a Broncos victory. So, here are my winners and los...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos just had the most Denver Broncos thrilling, memorable victory. They trailed 16-0 at halftime, and everything looked awful. Offense, defense, special teams, coaching, and everything else. A lifeless effort and a team that looked to be on the verge of yet another blowout loss on primetime.

As usual, that is exactly where the Broncos wanted them. From there, the Broncos would score 30 points in the second half and complete the thrilling comeback victory over the Rams.

There is A LOT to unpack from this up-and-down rollercoaster of emotions thriller that thankfully ended in a Broncos victory. So, here are my winners and losers from the Broncos' 30-26 victory over the Rams.

Like the game, we are starting with the bad.

The offense was bad, lifeless, and could not get anything going. The defense had no pass rush; they were whiffing on tackles again, and the Rams had no problem moving the ball on them. The special teams even struggled when usually reliable kicker Wil Lutz doinked one off the goalpost.

We were talking about Davis Webb giving up play calling again, talking about Vance Joseph's defense struggling against backs and tight ends, and they were trailing 16-0 at half against a good team and staring down a 1-2 record and another blowout loss on primetime.

It was bad, but we have to remember, this is the Denver Broncos.

They started out the second half with a predictable three-and-out right after an interview where Sean Payton said that series was a very important series for the team.

The defense would get the ball back, and then it was game on from there.

Touchdown to Nate Adkins , a crazy two-pointer by Jaylen Waddle , defense gets the ball back to the offense, touchdown and two-pointer to Pat Bryant , and suddenly, we have a tie game in the third quarter.

Rams would then drive down for a field goal to take a 3-point lead, but then it happened. Talanoa Hufanga CAUGHT THE BALL! Not only did he catch it, but he also took it back for a touchdown!

Holy shit, the Broncos are going to win this game!

Matthew Stafford said NOT SO FAST after Riley Moss was cooked on a double move, and the Rams would take a 26-23 lead. Those doubts started to creep back in as the Rams successfully took back the momentum, but again, remember. This is the Denver Broncos. What do the Denver Broncos do? They win football games in the 4th quarter.

Fourth-quarter magician Bo Nix led yet another 4th quarter comeback with chunk plays to Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin to get deep into Rams territory. After some controversial calls FINALLY fell in the Broncos' favor, Bo Nix called his number (twice) and would score what would end up being the game-winning touchdown.

Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, the Rams had time to go down and score a game-winning touchdown, and they got pretty damn close. Unfortunately for the Rams, Talanoa Hufanga learned how to catch a football, and on the final play of the game, as the clock hit zero, Hufanga would intercept Stafford for a second time and end the game.

Talanoa Hufanga cannot catch interceptions. He dropped like 10 last season and had two near picks early in this game. We pleaded, "PLEASE CATCH THE FOOTBALL," and the football gods listened and granted Hufanga the ability to catch.

He would go on to have a game-changing pick 6 of Matthew Stafford and later pick Stafford again in the end zone on the final play of the game, sealing the victory for the Broncos.

What a big-time effort by the Broncos' team leader. The Broncos did not force many turnovers last season, and they wanted to change that this season. We saw a game changing INT last week vs. the Jaguars and now, the Broncos had two big ones vs. the Rams.

If Hufanga can start coming down with these interceptions, he will put himself in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation.

Bryant was targeted a bunch in Week 1 but was mostly invisible in Week 2 while Jaylen Waddle was having his breakout performance. Well, he wasn't invisible tonight. He had just 2 targets, but he turned those 2 targets into 2 catches for 44 yards and 1 touchdown. He also caught one of the two Broncos' two-point conversions.

His second and final catch came on a 2nd-and-20 play with 3:25 left deep in their own territory. The Broncos were coming off a penalty, and things were looking bleak, but he would get open, and Nix would hit him for a 39-yard catch-and-run to set the Broncos up in field goal range.

Bryant would contribute later when he drew a controversial DPI on the Rams to give the Broncos an automatic first down and extend their drive. That drive would go on to end with what would end up being the game-winning touchdown.

The first half was ugly. He looked flustered and had two near-ugly interceptions, but that is just first-half Bo Nix. After halftime, second-half Bo Nix showed up and led the Broncos to three touchdown drives, including his game-winning QB sneak for the lead late in the 4th quarter.

Bo Nix now has 11 4th quarter comeback wins since 2024, which leads the NFL. It may not always be pretty; the analytical darlings hate him, the media disrespects him, but you cannot deny that Bo Nix is a gamer and has that magic to him.

When the Broncos scored their first touchdown and converted the two-point conversion, I knew the comeback was on. We have seen this script before, and Nix has ice water in his veins.

If he and the Broncos can ever put together a complete game, they could beat anyone at any time.

LOSER – CB Pat Surtain II: I do not type this often, and I believe it might be the first time that I have, but it's a fact. Davante Adams had Surtain's number tonight. PS2 is still an elite corner who will lock down opposing WRs more often than not, but tonight was not his night.

WINNER – TE Nate Adkins: Adkins caught his second touchdown of the season and now has a touchdown in back-to-back games. While the tight end position may not have an elite playmaker, if Adkins can score within the red zone, he can be a real weapon for this team.

WINNER – WR/KR Kolbe Katsis : It wasn't a perfect night for him, but he had a big return, which sparked the Broncos' comeback.

LOSER – LB Alex Singleton : Missed tackles, poor coverage, and more missed tackles. I noticed him much more in the first half, but it didn't seem like a strong night for him.

LOSER – CB Riley Moss: Moss has had a nice start to the season, but he had a rough one tonight. Most of the Broncos' corners struggled tonight, but Moss was called for an ugly DPI, gave up some plays throughout, and was burned on a double move for a long touchdown.

WINNER – Broncos pass rush: It did disappear at times, but it came alive in the second half and had 4 sacks of Matthew Stafford. Bonitto, Allen, Hufanga, and Uwazurike all combined for 4 sacks.

LOSER – WR Jaylen Waddle: He did have that nice two-point catch, but finished the night with 2 catches for 10 yards and had a couple of drops. The Rams had good coverage on him, but I was hoping for more from the Broncos' playmaking wide receiver.

LOSER – RB JK Dobbins : We simply need more from the Broncos' running back. He averaged 2.9 yards per carry tonight and struggled to get anything going consistently on the ground.

WINNER – Brandon Jones : He lacked the big impact play, but he was consistently around the ball and made good plays throughout. He was juked out of his socks by Kyren Williams once in the backfield, but shit happens.

WINNER – Red Zone offense: 3 for 3 after some struggles there vs. the Rams.

WINNER – Davis Webb, the play caller: His seat got hot again in the first half, but 3 touchdowns and two 2-pointers in the second half changed the tune a bit.

WINNER – Second-half adjustments: What a difference a half makes.

WINNER – Mile High crowd: They were loud again for a second straight week. Big home-field advantage.

LOSER – My health: This team is taking years off my life. What an emotional rollercoaster and thriller. Glad it ended with a win, though. Worth it.

articles.title: Davante Adams shreds Denver's secondary on Sunday night
articles.summary: In a high-profile matchup with Patrick Surtain II, Davante Adams turned 13 targets into seven catches fir 137 yards in Week 3.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams WR Davante Adams had seven receptions for 137 yards versus the Denver Broncos in Week 3. Adams was targeted a game-high 13 times.

Why It Matters: With Puka Nacua (groin) still unable to go, Adams again served as the primary option in LA's passing attack on Sunday night. And once again, he delivered. Just six days after lighting up the Giants for a 8-195-2 line, Adams made life miserable on Patrick Surtain II with 137 yards on seven receptions -- it could've been considerably more if Matthew Stafford hadn't misfired on a couple of balls where Adams had shaken Surtain. These last two games have proven that Adams can still produce like a WR1, both in the fantasy and NFL sense of the designation, but we'll have to wait and see what kind of regression we get when Nacua returns. Despite playing like a WR1 the past two games, Adams should be considered a WR2 until he shows he can put up similar numbers when Nacua is active.

articles.title: Khalil Shakir almost invisible in Week 3 against LA Chargers
articles.summary: Khalil Shakir held to six yards on one catch in Week 3 against LA Chargers.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills WR Khalil Shakir caught one of three targets for six yards in a Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers .

Why It Matters: Shakir was targeted 12 times with seven catches and 88 yards in the first two games, but he wasn't involved in this one. He doesn't get deep too often and only has four TDs since the start of 2025, keeping him a WR5 option. That will be the case again in Week 4 against the Patriots.
